d:
12 November 1947. India's first Diwali after Independence. But while millions prepared to celebrate freedom, millions more were struggling to survive the horrors of Partition.
Refugee camps were overflowing. Families had been separated. Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs had been forced to abandon their homes, and communal violence continued to scar a newly independent nation.
Just three days before Diwali, Mahatma Gandhi received a letter from a woman refugee suggesting that Indians should forget their sorrows and celebrate the country's first Diwali as a free nation. Gandhi disagreed.
